nom: NIVEA MEN Maximum Hydration Face Wash

segments.dry: Reviewers with dry, flaky skin, including one who bought it for his son's chronically dry nose and cheeks, report it relieves dryness and flaking without leaving skin feeling tight.
segments.sensitive: One reviewer prone to problematic, easily irritated skin found this the first affordable face wash that didn't leave his face irritated.

concerns.dehydration: The overwhelming majority of reviewers, including several with dry or dry, flaky skin, report the wash cleans thoroughly without leaving their face feeling tight, dry, or stripped, crediting the aloe vera with keeping skin soft and hydrated afterward; no reviewer reported it drying out their skin, though a few long-time users are wary that a recent reformulation may have diluted the original cleaning strength.
concerns.redness: A couple of reviewers report reduced redness after switching to this wash, including one whose post-shave cheek reddening disappeared and another whose dry-skin-related pink blotches cleared up.

aspects.libelle: Recent reformulation changed the scent, color, and thickness

extraits.titre: Nivea says same formula, but the ingredient concentrations have changed.
extraits.texte: Water, glycerin, denatured alcohol are the first three ingredients of the new clear formula. Then cocamidopropyl betaine (CAPB), which is the main surfactant in the formula, was second and now is fourth. Surfactants in soap increase the surface area and lathering ability of soaps. Higher surface area increases the chances of interacting with oils and other foreign material from the surface of one's skin so it can then rinse off. If you look at the last screenshot of the product you will see the older formula that lists glycerin as the 5th ingredient. As you know ingredients are listed by concentration, so they have increased the glycerin making it even more than their main surfactant. What you may not know is glycerin is a water-soluble filler that has no cleaning properties outside of being a "humectant"(a way to help keep skin hydrated) and keep the mixture thick. It is also much cheaper to buy as an ingredient thus "diluting" down the efficacy of the original formula at the balance of the "maximum hydration". What is the point of having oily moist skin? That is what I get from this and am sad after spending a long-time years ago looking for a compatible face soap that I know how to look for a new soap since this new formula stinks. Soap manufacturers have been adding in lotions and humectants for years at the cost of losing the main function of soap, which is cleaning the skin of oils and foreign materials. Stop diluting the soap!

I’m prone to problematic skin, so it was hard to find a great affordable face wash. I’ve tried many other brands, and my face still is still left irritated. This one is by far the best. This is the most soothing and moisturizing for my skin. It also works great after I shave my face. It lasts a while for the amount you get, so long as you don’t use more than you have to, which isn’t much. I also like that they took the coloring out of the ingredients. The only disappointment is I can’t find this in stores anymore because it’s either always out of stock or the place doesn’t sell it.

I'm using the scrub and the face wash before shave. There is a noticeable quality increase in shave, less skin irritation. I used to have reddening on the side of my cheek, now it's no longer there. Face is smooth and good looking. After shave I used a lotion, I have many, any lotion, for example old spice, and then nivia post shave balm. Face is smoother and more good looking than ever.
